standard_prerequisites.name: Projective neighbourhoods of a finite module flat at a point, in the henselian case
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-flat-finite-type-affine-neighbourhood-projective, invoked at proof line 5779
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives a fundamental system of affine open neighbourhoods of the point on which the global sections of the module are free over the base, which produces the filtered system of free modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: Universal injectivity of the transition maps, and the Mittag-Leffler criterion for a colimit of universally injective maps
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-universally-injective-local (proof line 5791); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-colimit-universally-injective-ML (proof line 5794)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first shows that the structure maps of the system are universally injective over the base, and the second converts that into the Mittag-Leffler property of the colimit.

core_obligations: Realise the module geometrically: find a finite type morphism and a point over the closed point with a finite type sheaf whose stalk at the point is the given module, and shrink so that every associated point of the special fibre specialises to that point (proof lines 5772-5778).

Produce the filtered system of free modules: by the projective neighbourhood statement there is a fundamental system of affine open neighbourhoods of the point on which the global sections of the sheaf are free over the base, and the module is their filtered colimit (proof lines 5779-5782).

Check the two conclusions: the reductions of the transition maps modulo the maximal ideal are injective because a section of the kernel would be supported away from the point, contradicting the choice of the neighbourhood; and since the transition maps are universally injective over the base, the colimit is Mittag-Leffler by the corresponding criterion (proof lines 5783-5794).
proof_roadmap: Realise the module geometrically and arrange the associated points (proof lines 5772-5778).
Get the filtered system of free modules from the projective neighbourhoods (proof lines 5779-5782).
Check injectivity of the reductions and conclude Mittag-Leffler (proof lines 5783-5794).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a finite flat module over an essentially finite type local map out of a henselian local ring is a filtered colimit of free modules whose transition maps induce injective maps modulo the maximal ideal, and is therefore Mittag-Leffler (statement lines 5758-5770, tag 05U7). The proof realises the module as the stalk of a finite type sheaf, arranges the associated points of the special fibre, uses the projective neighbourhood statement to get a fundamental system of affine neighbourhoods with free global sections, verifies injectivity of the reductions of the transition maps by a support argument, and applies the Mittag-Leffler criterion for colimits of universally injective maps. The support argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
